messages:
incident-bot: HIGH - Suspicious traffic: edge-service 'edge-proxy-2' is sending Authorization headers to analytics pipeline (kafka/topic: prod-telemetry). Sampled logs show full bearer tokens in payloads. Alert score 87. tagged: security, paging
jess_oncall: acked. I'm on pager. Can someone confirm scope? Is this limited to telemetry or also mirrored to external sinks?
liam_sre: looking... tailing recent collector logs now. grep shows ~3k events in last 10m with header payload. Preliminary: headers were included by new logging middleware rolled 02:17 UTC (ramped to 100% at 02:25).
nora_sec: thanks. tagging sec-response + legal. This looks like PII-style auth exposure. We need containment first: stop egress to analytics and rotate any potentially impacted tokens. Also capture sample for Triage channel (redacted).
trace_support: are customers impacted? any API calls observed with customer tokens?
liam_sre: unclear yet. The telemetry topic is internal analytics cluster (Kafka in prod-analytics). We see job-runner and web edge traffic forwarded. Need to enumerate which service accounts produced tokens vs user tokens.
leo_infra: I can pause the analytics consumer to stop writes from producer side (will cut analytics consumer group cg-telemetry-processor). Executing: `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka01:9092 --group cg-telemetry-processor --reset-offsets --to-latest --execute`
leo_infra: done — consumer paused. Producers still pushing to topic; I'll also add a network ACL to block egress to prod-analytics for edge-proxy-2: `aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress` (will apply).
jess_oncall: good. Leo — create a temporary WAF rule to strip Authorization headers at the edge for telemetry path /_telemetry/*. That prevents future leakage while we assess.
leo_infra: WAF rule staged and deployed (id: waf-evict-3951). Rule strips `Authorization` header for requests matching path `/api/v1/telemetry` and `/internal/telemetry/*`. Confirmed with a small test request — header removed.
ora_sec: containment in place. Next: identify token types. Are these service tokens (short-lived) or long-lived API keys? If service tokens, rotate affected service principals and rebuild trust.
liam_sre: grep of tokens shows multiple formats. Rough split: ~70% look like session JWTs (user-facing, short TTL), ~30% look like long-lived service keys (svc-). Sampled long-lived keys belong to analytics-ingest svc-account and a helper jobqueue daemon.
trace_support: user-facing JWT exposure — need customer notification plan if any tokens could be replayed. What's the TTL left on sampled JWTs?
ora_sec: pull a sample and check exp claim. Also check if any of those tokens were accepted by sensitive endpoints in the last 6 hours. If replay risk exists, we escalate to notifications.
jess_oncall: action items: 1) rotate long-lived service keys immediately (leo), 2) revoke and reissue any short-lived tokens that show >30m remaining, 3) search for any token reuse in auth logs (liam), 4) prepare hold-notice draft for customers if confirmed (trace/legal).
leo_infra: rotating svc keys for analytics-ingest and jobqueue now. Running `vault rotate -m svc/analytics-ingest` and `vault rotate -m svc/jobqueue`. ETA ~8m. I'll publish new creds to k8s secrets once rotation completes and trigger rolling deploys.
ora_sec: legal-team, please standby. We may need to preserve chain-of-custody for sampled logs. Don't purge the telemetry topic until forensic snapshot taken.
legal-team: acknowledged. We'll coordinate any required disclosures. Please tag exact timestamps and sample IDs.
liam_sre: scanning auth logs for token acceptance: running `pgrep | xargs` just kidding — actual query: `SELECT token_id, api, timestamp FROM auth_events WHERE token_value_hash IN (sample_hashes)`; started. If we find acceptance events outside normal client IPs we'll escalate.
ora_sec: also confirm whether telemetry cluster had any external connectors (S3/export) that could have forwarded logs out. If yes, isolate and snapshot connector state.
leo_infra: checked connectors: only internal ETL jobs consume cg-telemetry-processor; no external sinks configured. Still will snapshot offsets and store to secure vault.
trace_support: preparing customer impact note (internal draft): "We detected inadvertent logging of authentication headers to our internal analytics stream due to a telemetry middleware bug. We have contained exposure and are rotating affected keys. No evidence so far of external data exfiltration. We will notify if investigation finds customer tokens accepted outside normal patterns." Share draft to #security-notify for review.
jess_oncall: status update in 10. If auth-log scan finds replays, we'll escalate to incident-level pager and route to customer success. For now containment (WAF + pause consumers + rotate svc keys) complete; in-progress: auth replay scan, TTL checks on JWTs, forensic snapshot.
liam_sre: auth scan returned: 12 JWTs with >45m TTL found accepted by API from 5 distinct IPs matching normal ranges. No anomalous acceptances yet. Still correlating with external access logs.
ora_sec: keep forensics frozen. If any anomalies, immediate key revocation for affected apps and push-advisory. Also record mitigation timeline.
jess_oncall: thanks all. tagging this thread for follow-up. I'll create an incident ticket and assign remediation owners. :thumbsup:
